hook: A logging company can cut every tree on a 100-hectare hillside in a few weeks with a handful of machines. That is cheap timber. The next spring, the creek at the bottom of the hill runs brown after every rain and is several degrees warmer in summer, and the trout that lived there are gone.

options: The movement of soil and rock by water, wind or ice
The breakdown of rock in place by weather
The buildup of humus in the top layer of soil
The sinking of water into the ground
prereq.why: Erosion moves soil away; weathering breaks rock down in place.

prereq.q: How does warmer stream water affect dissolved oxygen?
options: Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen
Warmer water holds more dissolved oxygen
Temperature has no effect on dissolved oxygen
Warmer water holds oxygen only at night
prereq.why: Gases dissolve less in warm water, so warm water holds less oxygen for fish.

prereq.q: Forests store carbon mainly in which form?
options: Carbon in wood, leaves, roots and soil
Carbon dioxide gas held inside the trees
Methane gas trapped under the forest floor
Carbon only in the leaves that fall each year
prereq.why: Photosynthesis turns carbon dioxide into the carbon compounds of wood and other tissue.

figure.caption: The same hillside before and after clearcutting: without roots, litter and shade, more water and soil run off and the stream warms.

chain.cause: All trees on a slope are cut
chain.effect: roots die and leaf litter is removed, so the soil is bare
more water runs off and carries soil (sediment) into the stream

chain.cause: Sediment clouds the water and covers the gravel
chain.effect: less light reaches algae and fish eggs are smothered

chain.cause: The canopy no longer shades the stream
chain.effect: the water warms and holds less dissolved oxygen, so cold-water fish decline

ideas: Clearcutting removes all the trees in an area at once. It is cheap and fast, and some tree species that need full sun regrow well afterward.
Costs: soil erosion, sediment in streams, warmer streams with less dissolved oxygen, nutrients washed out of the soil, more runoff and flooding, and lost habitat.
Forests are a carbon sink. Cutting and burning or decaying the wood releases carbon dioxide, and the cleared land takes up less until trees regrow.
Deforestation is the lasting loss of forest, as when land is cleared for farms, pasture, mines or towns.

misconception.wrong: Trees store carbon dioxide, so cutting them lets that gas escape.
misconception.right: Trees store carbon, in wood, leaves and roots. When the wood burns or decays, that carbon combines with oxygen and enters the air as carbon dioxide.

summary: Clearcutting cuts every tree in an area: it is the cheapest way to harvest timber, but it bares the soil to erosion, fills streams with sediment, warms them so they hold less dissolved oxygen, washes out nutrients, and removes habitat and stored carbon. Deforestation is the lasting loss of forest to other land uses.
